results.title: King County Food Banks and Metro Routes - 2016
results.description:
This map originated as a King County Metro Comfort Station map, and I modified it for a class project. 

This map now contains a layer of King County Food Banks and their proximity to King County Metro routes. If the user clicks on the route, it will highlight and will show route information. If the user clicks the food bank, additional details (such as hours, communities served, and requirements) appear in the pop-up. 

Food bank operating hours and locations were verified as of 2/6/16, but the metro routes do change quarterly, and it is unclear to me if this map will automatically update. I will check it in a few weeks when the routes shift.
results.snippet: King County Food Banks identified along King County Transit Routes

results.name: GetAroundUDistrictCapitolHill.pdf
results.title: Get Around U-District and Capitol Hill
results.description:
Please scroll down for map viewing and download options.

Get Around Your Neighborhood!

Use this map to travel by bus, light rail, streetcar, bike and foot to visit interesting places and services in your neighborhood. Find out how close you are to parks, schools, libraries, local businesses, community services, and so much more! Leave your car at home and try a new way of getting around!

How to use this map

  1. If you live, work, or visit a location in the area, mark it on the map. Find other locations where you would like to travel. Look closely—there are many things to see and do just around the corner.
  2. Can you get there without a car?
    • Measure your trip by time instead of distance. You can get pretty far in a five minute walk and even farther by biking!
    • Bus routes and stops are marked. More bus information is often available at the stop or call 206-553-3000, check online or download an app to plan your trip: kingcounty.gov/metro
  3. Once you decide on your travel option head out and give it a try! Try a new way to travel once a day, week or month. Whatever works! Leaving the car behind is good for you, your neighborhood and the environment. Take your first step towards a healthier lifestyle.

How to view/download this map

PDF files

  • PDF file of the full two-page map brochure (28Mb file).
  • The following options provide smaller file sizes and each is a georeferenced PDF which gives mobile device users who have the free PDF Maps app the ability to locate themselves on the map in real time and do much more, such as record waypoints and photo locations, measure distances, and save and export map tracks. For each file, use the first link to open the PDF in a standard web browser (does not display well in Google Chrome) or copy and paste the PDF Maps link text into your PDF Maps app.
    • North map (13Mb): University District and UW campus, Green Lake, Wallingford, Roosevelt, Ravenna, Wedgwood, View Ridge, Bryant, and Laurelhurst.
      PDF Maps: pdfmap://aqua.kingcounty.gov/gis/web/Web/VMC/transportation/GetAround_UDistrictCapitolHill_North_GEO.pdf?title=Get%20Around%20U-District
    • North map - flat (5Mb): same but without terrain representation.
      PDF Maps: pdfmap://aqua.kingcounty.gov/gis/web/Web/VMC/transportation/GetAround_UDistrictCapitolHill_North_flat-GEO.pdf?title=Get%20Around%20U-District
    • South map (15Mb): UW campus, Montlake, Portage Bay, Eastlake, Madison Park, Capitol Hill, First Hill.
      PDF Maps: pdfmap://aqua.kingcounty.gov/gis/web/Web/VMC/transportation/GetAround_UDistrictCapitolHill_South_GEO.pdf?title=Get%20Around%20Capitol%20Hill
    • South map - flat (5Mb): same but without terrain representation.
      PDF Maps: pdfmap://aqua.kingcounty.gov/gis/web/Web/VMC/transportation/GetAround_UDistrictCapitolHill_South_flat-GEO.pdf?title=Get%20Around%20Capitol%20Hill

results.title: Transit Infrastructure
results.description:
While the City doesn't run the buses or light rail trains, we do work closely with King County Metro, Sound Transit, and other transit providers on major service and infrastructure changes within the city limits. We enhance transit through:

Transit Service. The Seattle Transit Measure (Proposition 1) provides funding for the City to purchase transit service from King County Metro. We also contribute funding for transit service on both streetcars with sponsorship funds, fare-box revenue, and other funding sources. 

Planning and Policy. We updated the Transit Master Plan in 2016 and regularly coordinate with Metro, Sound Transit, and other City departments on transit improvement projects and station area planning.

Seattle Streetcar. We own the South Lake Union and First Hill streetcar lines.  We contract with Metro for operations. Work on a streetcar line to connect the two existing lines is underway, read more about the Center City Connector project.

Corridor Improvements. Levy to Move Seattle (a voter-approved levy) provides funding for transit corridor improvements, including seven new RapidRide corridors. We plan and build street, signal, bus stop facility, and technology improvements that increase bus speeds and enhance passenger comfort along key corridors. View current capital projects.
results.snippet: This map is part of the map series for the Complete Streets Review process.  Included in this map is data that will help project managers understand the transit needs around thier project.
